reason: The septum fits the unpartitioned heart chambers and separates the two sides before connecting their routes.
expectation: The heart will gain a partition between its right and left sides.

effect: The septum divided the heart and revealed separate inlet and outlet valve slots.
reaction: The reference panel makes the need for valves clear.
reason: The inlet valves match the ventricular inlet slot.
expectation: The inlet valves will fit between the upper and lower chambers.

effect: The inlet valves are fitted and prevent backward flow toward the atria during ventricular contraction.
reaction: The filling and squeezing frames clarify their one-way action.
reason: The outlet valves match the remaining ventricular outlet slot.
expectation: The outlet valves will fit at the ventricular exits.

effect: Both valve sets are fitted, completing the first goal; the outlet valves limit return from the arteries between beats.
reaction: The contrast between valve action during ejection and between beats is clear.
reason: Conducting tissue should provide the electrical coordination needed for the divided heart to pump.
expectation: The heart will gain a pacemaker and conducting pathways to coordinate its contractions.

effect: The heart now has conducting pathways that coordinate atrial and ventricular contractions.
reaction: The timed wave makes the order of contraction clear.
reason: The pulmonary loop visibly connects the right heart to the lungs and returns to the left heart.
expectation: The pulmonary vessels will connect the two sides of the heart through the lung capillaries.

effect: The pulmonary route now links the right heart to lung capillaries and returns to the left atrium, leaving the body route open.
reaction: The separate routes are becoming clear.
reason: The systemic vessel network matches the open connection toward body tissues.
expectation: The systemic vessels will connect the heart to tissue capillaries and back.

effect: The heart is now connected to both pulmonary and systemic vessel loops.
reaction: The two routes are now in place.
reason: The heart’s own vessels should supply its muscular wall.
expectation: Coronary vessels will connect to the circulation and supply the heart muscle.

alternatives.reason: Blood also needs to enter the connected routes.

effect: Coronary vessels now branch from the aorta to supply heart muscle and return blood mainly to the right atrium.
reaction: The distinction between chamber blood and the heart muscle’s own supply is useful.
reason: Blood is the remaining component needed to fill the connected circulation.
expectation: Blood will circulate through the heart and its pulmonary, systemic and coronary routes.

effect: Blood now fills the connected circulation, completing the goal and showing the pulmonary and systemic routes as separate loops.
reaction: The arrows make the overall route easy to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the heart’s own vessels was most worthwhile: the planned cutaway distinguishes blood in the chambers from the coronary supply needed by the thick heart muscle.

leastWorthwhile.text: Joining the systemic network was comparatively predictable, and its result added little explanation beyond showing the two loops.

surprise.text: The coronary route’s return mainly through the coronary sinus to the right atrium added a detail I had not expected.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the valve slots and vessel descriptions made the sequence understandable.

continue.text: I would continue: tracing the separate routes and the heart muscle’s own supply made the construction educational, though the assembly was often straightforward.
